summary: Typosquat exfiltrates Kubernetes service-account token, env secrets and container-escape recon to hardcoded attacker domain
details: css-overscroll-contain@1.0.2 is published as a CSS overscroll-behavior polyfill with an empty index.js, but ships thunderboltRegistry.js whose module exports register several host names matching Wix Thunderbolt internal registries (thunderboltRegistry, siteAssetsRegistry, documentManagementRegistry, editorRegistry, corvidRegistry, dataBindingRegistry, thunderboltBuilderRegistry, thunderboltPreviewRegistry); registry-manifest.min.json aliases every one of these to the same payload file. On require, a top-level IIFE in thunderboltRegistry.js runs recon commands via child_process.execSync (id, uname, FD/socket maps, mountinfo, cgroup release_agent writes, mknod of cuse/fuse/sda, user+mount namespace unshare, perl memfd_create+exec via /proc/self/fd), reads /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, and greps the process environment for variables matching KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/AUTH/URL/ENDPOINT. Each result is POSTed via https.get to the hardcoded attacker endpoint https://dxpoc.gt.tc/callback.php/bb8968d0f67000433bf7005dd5ad2d1f. The package's declared purpose is a cover story; the exported registry names are shaped to be resolved by Wix's internal registry loader so the beacon fires inside Wix build/runtime infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
